ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Irrespective of the partnership's pass-through tax status, every partner, UBO, signatory, and senior advisor must be screened before admission against the FINTRAC sanctions and politically exposed persons (PEP) framework, the OFAC SDN list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, Canada's Special Economic Measures Act and Regulations, and the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, RSC 2001, c 27, s 35. Enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds verification, beneficial-ownership pyramiding, negative-media assessment, and adverse-legal-links review, is mandatory for the study-abroad and immigration visa consulting sector.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Registre des entreprises (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French-language name doctrine is mandatory under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11. A Quebec limited partnership must bear a French legal designation, namely 'société en commandite' or the abbreviation 's.e.c.'; the operative name must be drafted in French or, if a proper name or recognized foreign trademark is used, transliterated consistently into Latin script and compliant with Quebec trademark and linguistic rules. An English-only name is not accepted unless an exception is granted for the applicant's family name or a foreign registered trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registraire rejects a proposed name, the applicant must first file a written request for reconsideration with the Direction de l'avis de non-opposition within 30 days of the refusal, attaching a revised French-language name, a marketing search report, and, where applicable, consent from the holder of the conflicting prior name. If the reconsideration is refused, the applicant may contest the decision before the Tribunal administratif du Québec under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss 7 and 8. A name reservation may be renewed once before expiry, but renewal is granted only if no third-party opposition has been filed in the interim.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional and limited. A virtual office is permitted for the Quebec limited partnership only if it consists of a physical, continuously staffed address in Quebec at which legal documents may be served and records are kept; a mail-forwarding-only or PO-box address is not acceptable. Because the commercial activity is study-abroad placement and immigration/visa advisory, the immigration consultant regulator will require real premises for client intake and interview files, making a purely virtual arrangement inadequate for full licensing and commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 45% – medium-high risk of unannounced on-site inspection by the Registraire des entreprises and the Quebec immigration consultant licensing body, given the consumer-facing nature of visa advisory, the use of escrow payment rails, and the enhanced AML/CFT monitoring classification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CQLR c. CCQ-1991), arts. 2186 and 2236–2246 (limited partnership / société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), ss. 2, 4, 23–29; Regulation respecting the fees payable under that Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), operating within Revenu Québec and accessible through the Services Québec / CliquezAffaires online portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) filed in the Registre des entreprises du Québec.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required under the Civil Code of Québec for a limited partnership; capital contributions are freely agreed in the limited partnership agreement. No statutory escrow account is filed with the Registrar, but CICC practice rules require client funds to be held in a segregated trust or escrow account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the General Partner, acting on behalf of the limited partnership to be organized under articles 2236 et seq. of the Civil Code of Québec, subscribes to the General Partner's full partnership interest and approves the limited partnership agreement. FURTHER RESOLVED: That the registered and head office of the limited partnership shall be established at [Québec address] and the Registraire des entreprises shall be instructed to file the declaration of registration. FURTHER RESOLVED: That [name], a Québec resident, is appointed manager and sole authorized representative, with full authority to open escrow and bank accounts and execute all statutory filings. These resolutions are effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online name search and reservation via the Services Québec / CliquezAffaires portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a prior name search in the Registre des entreprises du Québec and the Canadian trademark database using the REQ online tool. Submit an optional name-reservation request to lock a distinctive name; verify French-language conformity of the name under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11); ensure a commercial office address is zoned for permitted use.
required_dossiers: Signed consent of all partners to the proposed partnership name
List of proposed general and limited partners
Proof of address of the proposed head office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, remove prohibited terms, add a distinctive element, and resubmit; the REQ cures struck applications through a notice-and-amendment loop without additional filing fee for a single resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement (Contrat de société en commandite)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private execution among partners; no filing at this stage, agreement kept with partnership records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute a written limited partnership agreement under arts. 2186 and 2236–2246 of the Civil Code of Québec, allocating contributions of limited partners and management powers of the general partner; record profit-sharing ratios, transfer restrictions, dissolution triggers, and the head-office clause; optional notarized execution for third-party evidentiary certainty.
required_dossiers: KYC/AML identification file for each partner
Capital contribution acknowledgment or escrow instruction letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any partner objection is cured by private amendment and re-execution; the Registrar is not involved at this step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing the Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — online filing via Revenu Québec's Mon dossier d'entreprise / CliquezAffaires electronic service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online declaration of registration: enter the partnership's exact name, Quebec head-office address, general partner's particulars, limited partners' identities where prescribed, and the formation date; pay the statutory fee (approx. CAD 52); the REQ issues the Numéro d'entreprise du Québec (NEQ) and a registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized or certified identification of the general partner
Proof of Quebec head-office address (lease or instrument of title)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire issues a notice of deficiency (avis de défaut), provide the missing particulars within the regulatory delay, generally 30 days; a refused declaration is cured by filing a corrected declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Payroll Registration with Revenu Québec and CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (QST, source deductions) and Canada Revenue Agency (GST/HST program account)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ, activate the Revenu Québec 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' account; register for QST and, if hiring staff, payroll source-deduction accounts; register the GST/HST account with CRA; register as an employer with CNESST; open a designated trust/escrow account compliant with CICC trust accounting rules before receiving client funds.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration attracts penalties under the QST Act and the Excise Tax Act; cure by voluntary disclosure and a penalty-relief application to Revenu Québec or CRA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC); municipal permits office; CNESST (occupational health and safety)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For remunerated immigration, study-abroad placement, or visa advisory services, obtain a Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) licence for each advising practitioner, or ensure services are rendered through a member of the Barreau du Québec or Chambre des notaires; obtain a municipal business permit and occupancy/fire-safety certificate for the office premises; register the workplace with CNESST and post required occupational health and safety signage.
required_dossiers: CICC licence application or attestation of membership
CNESST employer registration and workplace hazard assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A CICC deficiency notice may be satisfied by resubmission within the prescribed period; municipal permit denials are curable by zoning compliance or a minor-variance application (dérogation mineure).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC) under the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants Act (S.C. 2019, c. 29, s. 292); Quebec counterpart: Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI) for Quebec-selection and investor-program advisories; Barreau du Québec and Chambre des notaires for service rendered by legal professionals.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultant (RCIC) licence — Certificat de consultant en immigration du Canada (CICC registration)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — professional office use; no trigger under Schedule I of the Environmental Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for office operations; sanitary effluent must comply with municipal sewer bylaws and the Regulation respecting wastewater disposal systems; no industrial VOCs or hazardous waste streams; electronic waste disposal must follow Recyc-Québec directives.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-prevention inspection certificate from the competent municipal fire service under the Québec Safety Code; structural and occupancy clearance under the Québec Construction Code (CQLR c. B-1.1, r. 5); CNESST employer and workplace registration and hazard assessment under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c. S-2.1).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — national portal 'My Business Account' (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html); Revenu Québec — provincial portal 'Business Services Online' / CléNumérique (https://www.revenuquebec.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Register the Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite) with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to obtain the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). 2. Apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) using Form RC1 or the 'Register a Business with the CRA' online service, and open a GST/HST program account when taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000. 3. Register separately with Revenu Québec for Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and, if applicable, employer source-deduction/QPIP/CNESST accounts using Form RM-2 or the online CléNumérique service. 4. The LP retains pass-through status: it does not pay income tax at the entity level, but it must file partnership information returns T5013 (Federal) and TP-600 (Québec) and issue T5013/RL-15 allocation slips to partners. Non-resident partners must obtain a Canadian individual tax number (ITN) using Form NR/T1 or T1 adjustment procedures, and may be subject to Canadian withholding tax on allocable Canadian-source income absent treaty relief.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists in Canada; entity classification follows statutory income tax law. A Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent by statute. Relevant mechanisms: (a) the partnership may elect, in certain continuity events, to be deemed a Canadian partnership under Income Tax Act subsection 96(9); (b) a non-resident partner may elect under section 216 of the Income Tax Act to file and pay tax on net Canadian rental income, or claim treaty-reduced withholding; (c) hybrid mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act automatically deny deductions or recharacterize actions where a fiscally transparent entity such as the LP creates differential cross-border tax outcomes for foreign partners. No election is available for an LP to be taxed as a corporation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST); a non-harmonized dual value-added tax regime in Quebec, administered jointly by CRA and Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies from carrying on a commercial activity in Canada over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; the same CAD 30,000 threshold applies for QST registration with Revenu Québec. Non-residents and LPs supplying only zero-rated export services may register voluntarily to claim input tax/input tax refunds even if below threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory transaction-level e-invoicing API. GST/QST registrants must issue invoices containing prescribed data (supplier name and BN/GST/QST numbers, invoice date, description, tax amounts). Electronic invoices are permissible when the records are reliable and auditable. Revenu Québec imposes electronic filing mandates for certain payroll returns but not for GST/QST transaction pre-approval.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of services by the LP to a non-resident client may be zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act if the recipient is a non-resident and the service is not in respect of real or tangible personal property situated in Canada and is not performed in Canada for consumption in Canada. For the study-abroad and golden-visa residential advisory business, contemporaneous evidence must establish: a written contract with a non-resident client; delivery of the advisory work offshore (e.g., meetings, analytics and visa-application preparation undertaken from the client's home jurisdiction); invoices issued to the foreign payor; and cross-border wire remittance. Services physically performed in Canada, such as in-person representation or filings carried out in Quebec before immigration authorities, are generally treated as supplied in Canada and attract full GST/QST; such supplies may fall outside zero-rating. Zero-rated supplies are taxable supplies and entitle the LP to recover input tax credits and input tax refunds for GST/QST incurred on related inputs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Form B13A Canadian Export Declaration / CBSA Customs Export Declaration and carrier outward manifest where physical goods are exported
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing departure from Canada and destination abroad for any tangible property
Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign exchange bank remittance advice demonstrating receipt of export proceeds from a non-resident client
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess within the normal four-year limitation period, or beyond in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or neglect, and disallow zero-rating if export substantiation is incomplete or the 180-day cross-border remittance record is deficient. The LP may then be reassessed for unpaid GST/QST, with statutory interest at the prescribed daily rate (e.g., 9% simple per annum for 2025, adjustable) and penalties. Gross negligence penalties can reach 25% of the tax sought to be avoided, and wilful evasion may trigger criminal prosecution under section 327 of the Excise Tax Act, resulting in substantial fines and imprisonment for directors/managing partners.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange monitoring and AML/ATF administration jointly conducted by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); prudential supervision of banks by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible for both current and capital account purposes. Canada has not maintained exchange control legislation since the Foreign Exchange Control Orders lapsed in 1951. Profit remittance, partner distributions, and capital repatriation by non-resident partners of a Quebec Limited Partnership are unrestricted from an FX perspective. The only operative constraints are Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (default 25% on distributions from a pass-through partnership unless treaty-reduced), PCMLTFA reporting duties for international electronic fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, and sanctions screening under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act. The Quebec LP should not expect any FX approval gate for inbound capital or outbound client settlements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation deadline for export proceeds or service fee receipts. Foreign currency receipts may be freely retained in USD, EUR, GBP, or other currencies, converted at negotiated bank rates, or applied directly to outbound settlements. The only compliance layers are FINTRAC ETR threshold reporting, record-keeping of FX conversion contracts, and applicable economic sanctions screening before any cross-border movement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — viable only as an ancillary disbursement channel, not as a primary treasury or regulatory escrow repository. Non-bank digital payment providers operating in Canada are classified as money services businesses (MSBs) requiring FINTRAC registration under the PCMLTFA; providers active in Quebec must additionally hold a money-services business registration with the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF). Global EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) clear CAD exclusively through partner Schedule I banks and are not chartered banks; therefore they cannot lawfully hold client funds in escrow for immigration advisory engagements, which under the CICC (College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants) rules must be isolated in a regulated trust or escrow account. EMIs may be used for low-value operational payouts, foreign university tuition disbursements, and supplier settlements after full counterparty verification, subject to a documented prohibition on mixing client deposits.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally permitted where the Quebec LP has a Canadian-resident general partner or a Canadian corporate co-general partner and the registered office is confirmed through the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) attestation. Authorized signatories can complete onboarding through video interviews, notarized or commission-certified true copies, and bank-grade e-signature. However, if all general partners are non-resident individuals or foreign corporations, most Schedule I banks require an in-person compliance interview for the responsible officer and may demand a physical inspection of the registered address, adding 30-60 days of review. Recommended structure: appoint a Canadian-resident individual or Canadian corporation as general partner, prepare apostilled corporate resolutions and certified passport copies for every non-resident limited partner, and bring original documentation to a Montreal or Toronto branch to accelerate the enhanced due diligence process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners creating opaque beneficial ownership through the LP pass-through structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed limited partnership agreement identifying each partner capital participation; REQ certificate of registration; certified copies of incorporation documents of all non-resident corporate partners; bank-issued good-standing letters from foreign counterparty banks; a FINTRAC-compliant beneficial ownership register identifying ultimate individuals holding 25% or more; notarized declarations of source of wealth and source of funds for each capital contribution; and a transaction-flow narrative mapping every contributor to a physical bank account in an OECD or G20 jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border incoming wires from applicant countries for study-placement and immigration visa service fees, perceived as money-laundering or fraud exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CICC membership certificate and confirmation of Quebec regulatory compliance; executed client service agreements; itemized invoices distinguishing government application fees, university tuition deposits, and advisory service fees; a dedicated escrow agreement and trust ledger proving no commingling; bank statements demonstrating predictable and documented client flows; sanctions and PEP screening logs per client; and a written suspension policy for wires lacking a stated purpose or student reference identifier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow account disbursements to third-party beneficiaries (foreign universities, immigration authorities, and overseas sub-agents) triggering sanctions false positives or structuring flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Regulatory escrow terms approved by Canadian legal counsel; an authorization-and-disbursement matrix limited to named beneficiaries; signed contracts with each university or sub-agent including full legal identity and jurisdiction; sanctions screening calibration records covering the Canadian Consolidated List, UNSC lists, and OFAC lists; client-level source-of-funds verification files; transaction logs showing round-dollar disbursements consistent with contractual milestones; and a false-positive remediation procedure with customer-substantiation templates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Clientele risk indicator: study-abroad applicants originating from FATF high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence file per client, including passport, study permit or visa application record, university admission letter, 12-month bank statements or guaranteed investment certificate evidencing financial ability, and a signed PEP declaration; documented jurisdiction risk-scoring methodology; segmented onboarding limits with mandatory escalation for high-risk countries; independent adverse-media search results; internal AML policy manual; and an annual independent AML review commissioned from an OSFI- or FINTRAC-recognized consultant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing uses SWIFT MT103 for customer-initiated transfers and MT202 for interbank cover, with the domestic CAD leg settling over Payments Canada LVTS or the emerging Real-Time Rail for same-day value. Wire instructions must name the Quebec LP as beneficiary with descriptive text 'Capital contribution — partnership equity — ISIC 7810 advisory services' and reference the capital-call schedule. FINTRAC requires banks to report incoming international electronic fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more within five business days; the LP must simultaneously preserve capital-call notices, GP resolutions authorizing each contribution, and identity evidence for each foreign partner. Banks commonly hold inbound funds for a one-to-five business day confirmation window and may request proof of source of funds in the form of foreign bank statements before releasing funds to operations or escrow.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is the SWIFT MT103 for customer trade settlements covering university tuition deposits, immigration government fee reimbursements, sub-agent commissions, and refunds. For transactions exceeding approximately CAD 1,000,000 or contractually guaranteed obligations, a commercial letter of credit under UCP 600 issued by a Canadian Schedule I bank may be used, although for ISIC 7810 advisory services MT103 is the prevailing standard. Every outbound wire is sanctions-screened; outbound international ETRs of CAD 10,000 or more are reported to FINTRAC. Banks require supporting invoice copies, a disbursement authorization signed by the general partner, and, for escrow releases, evidence matching the escrow agreement. When payment must be made in a foreign currency, the bank executes an offsetting spot FX conversion and settles through the corresponding-correspondent network rather than a separate rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable over-the-counter FX forwards (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP, CAD/AUD) with Canadian Schedule I banks or OSFI-regulated counterparties under ISDA/CSA or standard bank master forward agreements
FX options (plain vanilla European-style calls and puts on CAD crosses) for contingent future obligations such as client refund liabilities
Cross-currency swaps (fixed-for-floating or floating-for-floating) for term-converting tuition deposit liabilities or phased non-resident partner capital repatriation
FX swaps and swap-style rollovers extending forward positions without mark-to-market renegotiation

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not necessary or standard for CAD given full convertibility; Canadian banks quote deliverable forwards with settlement in CAD and are the compliant market convention

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) for the Limited Partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of the initial registration of the LP; online filing by the general partner.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 30 per month up to a maximum of CAD 300; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off from the Quebec registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (income allocation to partners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of the fifth month following the partnership fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 fiscal year-end due May 31).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of CAD 100 per partner per day, capped at CAD 2,500 for small partnerships (1-2 partners); for larger partnerships the cap rises to CAD 7,500; additional penalties apply for inaccurate allocations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: TP-600 Partnership Information Return (Québec provincial allocation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the partnership fiscal year-end (e.g., December 31 fiscal year-end due June 30).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 500 plus interest; repeated defaults may lead to seizure of amounts owed and additional zealous-nexus assessments.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is required for a private non-offering Limited Partnership under Quebec's Civil Code unless: (a) the partnership agreement expressly mandates an audit; (b) the partnership holds client immigration/escrow trust funds, in which case an annual trust account audit by a Quebec-licensed CPA is required; or (c) the partnership exceeds CAD 20 million in gross revenue and is financially significant under the Quebec Accountancy Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises, CPA Canada Handbook Part II) applies by default; IFRS (Part I) is required if the LP is a 'reporting' entity. For income tax allocation purposes, financial statements must be prepared on the same basis and GIFI schedules attached to T5013/TP-600.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, the LP's annual declaration to the REQ must identify all ultimate beneficiary owners (UBOs), including any transfer of limited partnership interests during the preceding year. A transfer of 25% or more of interests must be reported immediately via an interim filing (Form 2-UBO), and the register of limited partners must be updated permanently. Delayed disclosure may result in a penalty of CAD 25 per day of non-compliance.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of limited partners (name, capital contribution, share of profits, transfer history)
Register of general partners and capital contributions
Minute book and resolutions of partner meetings
Register of ultimate beneficial owners (UBO) with annual attestation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% entity-level for the limited partnership (flow-through); reference combined federal+Quebec general corporate rate: 26.5% (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory holiday or preferential deduction for the LP itself. Partner-level incentives may include the Canadian-controlled private corporation small business deduction if the partner is a qualifying CCPC, and any eligible SR&ED tax credits. The ISIC 7810 study-abroad/immigration-consulting sector has no sector-specific Quebec tax abatement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return, transmitted electronically via CRA-approved EFILE software or a registered tax preparer through the CRA My Account portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five months after the partnership's fiscal period end. For a December 31 fiscal period end, the T5013 is due by May 31 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's share of current-year partnership net income or loss arising from immigration visa consulting and international student placement services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the Canadian-source portion of partnership income allocable to the non-resident partner. The T5013 must separately identify all non-resident partners and show the amount subject to Part XIII withholding under ITA s.212(2.1).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner's share of taxable capital gains and capital losses from partnership property dispositions, including any gains on taxable Canadian property.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, include only gains from dispositions that constitute taxable Canadian property; cross-reference to the NR4 slip for withheld taxes on the gain.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete legal name, Social Insurance Number / Canadian Business Number or foreign tax identification number, residency status, profit/loss allocation percentage, and partner type (general or limited).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident partner, state country of residence, provide the applicable treaty residency certificate reference, and indicate whether the partner claims a reduced DTA withholding rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: CRA late-filing penalty under ITA s.162(7)-(7.2): C$25 per day to a maximum of C$2,500 per return, plus C$125 per week for failure to issue T5013 slips (maximum C$2,500). Quebec equivalent under the Taxation Act: daily penalty C$25 to C$2,500, plus statutory interest on unreported partner allocations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Relevé 15 (RL-15) - Amounts Paid to a Partner in a Partnership, filed electronically through Revenu Québec's SDL transmission system or certified third-party software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The RL-15 is generally filed by the last day of the fifth month following the partnership's fiscal period end, consistent with the federal T5013 deadline; for a December 31 period end, due May 31.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner's share of the partnership's net income (loss) for Quebec income tax purposes, including business income from immigration advisory services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete Box A only to the extent the non-resident partner is subject to Quebec provincial tax on that allocation; otherwise indicate the partner's non-residency status and the applicable treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner's share of taxable capital gains or losses recognized by the partnership during the fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, report Quebec-source capital gains only where the partner would be taxable under the Taxation Act on the disposition of taxable Quebec property.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec may impose C$25 per day (minimum C$250, maximum C$2,500) for a missing RL-15, and an additional penalty of C$50 per week for late issuance after the initial 30-day grace period, up to C$2,500, plus interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: N/A - a limited partnership does not pay dividends. Profit repatriation to partners is effected through allocation of partnership income/drawings. Non-resident partners' share of Canadian-source partnership income is subject to Part XIII withholding at the statutory rate of 25%, unless a DTA reduces that rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before remitting an allocation to a non-resident partner, the partnership must obtain a valid Certificate of Residency / Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the partner's tax authority and any required Canadian treaty-relief form (e.g., Form NR301, if applicable). The partner must be the beneficial owner and satisfy any limitation-on-benefits clause. The reduced withholding rate is applied only when the treaty claim is properly documented on or before the remittance date; retrospective adjustments require a refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate: 25% for royalties paid to non-residents. Interest paid at arm's length to a non-resident creditor is generally exempt from Canadian withholding tax under ITA s.212(1)(b)(vii); non-arm's length interest and participating debt interest are subject to 25% statutory withholding. Under the Canada-U.S. tax treaty, royalties are commonly reduced to 10% (15% for certain cultural/copyright licenses), and interest may be reduced to 0-15% depending on the nature of the interest and the creditor's status.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: ITA s.247 does not specify a fixed dollar threshold for TP documentation. CRA administrative policy requires contemporaneous documentation when the aggregate fair market value of non-arm's length cross-border transactions exceeds C$1 million in a taxation year. Large taxpayers with annual gross revenue exceeding C$50 million must prepare and provide a Local File and Master File consistent with OECD TP Guidelines.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no dedicated Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) comparable to offshore financial centres. Instead, the CRA deploys the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (ITA s.245) and transfer-pricing recharacterization (ITA s.247(2)) to disregard transactions lacking genuine commercial substance. Revenu Québec's Taxation Act s.1079 contains an analogous anti-avoidance rule. For a CICC-regulated immigration consultancy, physical premises in Quebec, real employees, client-facing operations, and business records are key indicators of economic substance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a false T5013 or intentionally allocating Canadian-source partnership income to a non-resident partner without applying the 25% Part XIII withholding, with intent to evade Canadian income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Indictable tax evasion under ITA s.239(1): fine of 50% to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment for up to 5 years. False-statements civil penalty under ITA s.163(2): 10% or 50% (gross negligence) of the understated amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers of the corporate general partner are jointly and severally liable for the LP's unremitted Part XIII withholding under ITA s.227.1(1), including interest and penalties. CRA can issue director liability certificates and enforce recovery against personal assets, and in egregious cases lay criminal charges against directing minds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing study-abroad or visa/residency advisory services for a fee without being a member of the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC) or without the required Quebec provincial authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the CICC Act (SC 2019, c.29): on indictment, a fine of up to C$50,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 2 years; on summary conviction, a fine of up to C$10,000 and/or imprisonment for 6 months. Quebec licensing bodies may also issue administrative fines and cease-and-desist orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or general partners who direct, authorize, or benefit from unlicensed practice may be prosecuted as parties to the offence under s.21 Criminal Code, and are personally liable for disgorgement of fees and restitution to affected clients.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a Quebec limited partnership with no office, employees, or substantive business activity, used solely as a conduit to invoice immigration consulting fees and shift profits to non-residents or to a low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA can reallocate income to the true economic owner under ITA s.247(2), disallow the loss of the partnership structure under GAAR (s.245), and impose a penalty under s.163(2.1) for misstatements attributable to the GAAR, generally 15% of the benefit obtained.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Limited partners who participate in management of the LP lose their limited-liability shield and become jointly liable. Directors of the corporate general partner may be held personally liable for the reassessed tax and penalties if they knowingly permitted a sham structure; CRAs can also obtain court injunctions requiring winding-up.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting client funds via escrow or wire transfer for tuition fees, visa processing, or immigration services without registering with FINTRAC as a Money Services Business, where the business is engaged in remitting or transmitting money, or failing to implement a complete AML/CTF compliance program.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, up to C$1 million per violation for MSBs; criminal fines and imprisonment for knowingly dealing in funds derived from crime or for intentionally avoiding FINTRAC registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers and directors who participate in, direct, or consent to a FINTRAC violation are personally liable for the administrative monetary penalty; courts may also order restitution, compliance audits, and injunctions freezing firm assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Counseling, aiding, or helping a client misrepresent financial standing, residence history, or immigration documents to obtain a Quebec selected certificate, study permit, or 'Golden Visa' permanent residence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under IRPA s.127(b), knowingly making a false representation is an offence punishable by a fine up to C$100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years. The client additionally becomes inadmissible to Canada for misrepresentation for 5 years, and the consultancy's CICC licence may be revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or the general partner who orchestrate or supervise the misrepresentation are personally liable as 'authorized representatives', subject to criminal prosecution, disgorgement of fees, civil claims from the visa applicant, and a permanent ban from the CICC.
